source.state: Current uncommitted working tree; rendering source SHA-256 below. The isolated 35.72 FPS measurement predates the final deferred shadow-override disposal fix. The current-code retest below was contended by iRacing; it is not a clean performance comparison.

method.route: 3 laps, forest/open/coast, 12 seconds per view, including final streaming completion.
method.isolation: Fresh temporary headless Chrome profile on RTX 5060; no concurrent browser tests, builds, encoders or benchmark runs during the accepted run. Ordinary desktop/background activity not eliminated.
method.timing: Frame interval percentiles exclude the first sample, which begins before recording. Average FPS counts submitted frames over the browser-clock recording window, including final tile loading. This is not display scanout or GPU completion rate.

profiling.original: Cold forest/open CPU sampling: about 204.6 s (82.5%) in node shader building, including 143.1 s in shadow rendering. Synchronous GPU pipeline-creation calls accounted for only a small part; this does not measure asynchronous driver work.
profiling.shaderProbe: After removing opaque shadow surface evaluation, cold-forest main terrain shader builds still numbered 44. Shared graph plus attribute-based terrain geomorph reduced this to one.
profiling.warm: An intermediate 8.45 s warmed-forest profile located remaining CPU costs in shadow material/geometry keys, matrix updates and draw submission. The final pass adds stable shadow overrides and one transform update per composed frame.

changes: Share materials across spatial foliage batches; drive stable LOD fade shaders with attributes.
Use geometry-owned native instance attributes and per-renderer proxies.
Share terrain graphs per texture-array set with independent material/shore values and attribute-based native geomorph.
Exclude opaque surface evaluation from shadow alpha.
Keep shadow overrides stable per material/light; update transforms once per composed frame.
Defer override disposal until source dispose listeners complete, preventing duplicate cleanup of shared shadow buffers.

verification.browser: Targeted RTX Chrome: native composition/baking/GLB export/resize/resource cycles; unavailable GPU; prepared world streaming/unloading; 50 foliage batches, independent matrix updates and two renderers; independent tile palettes/morphs, WebGL silhouette parity and surviving-tile disposal; complementary LOD cutouts/directional and six-face point shadows; leaf transmission on both backends; repeated live shadow-caster removal; foliage/surface failure injection, retry, undo/redo and persistence.
verification.scope: Not a full browser-suite rerun. Dense populations of the supplied high-polygon banana asset, editor FPS, input latency, Linux/software and other hardware were not benchmarked in this pass.

excluded: Short prototype timings and a final attempt interrupted to remove overlap with a finishing browser test are excluded.
limits: Submitted traversal FPS is not physical display rate or warmed stationary/editor FPS.
The original native run skipped route phases due to stalls; requested route is the same but executed camera samples differ.
The pre-port WebGL renderer has different Three/shading/compositing implementations; this is not an API speed comparison.
GPU timestamp coverage differs between backends; no cross-backend GPU-time claim.
Steady 30 FPS remains unproven unless the frame-time acceptance flag passes.
Private Three r186 adapters need review on dependency upgrades.
The isolated optimized run predates the final shadow-disposal correction; current code has correctness coverage but its retest was contended by iRacing.

currentCodeRetest.limitation: iRacingSim64DX11 was active after this run. Post-run RTX utilization was 68%, and iRacing consumed 2.77 CPU seconds in an approximately one-second sample. It was not terminated. This final-code timing is confounded by external CPU/GPU work and must not replace an idle-system comparison.
